title: Improve cold-flow accuracy, curved stress balance and full-update robustness
description: The bounded conservative MHD reference is verified, but the independent double rarefaction has 114 percent central pressure error at nz640 despite converging bulk L1 errors and inactive positivity limiting. Curved-equilibrium force RMS converges at about order 1.5. Improve and quantify these errors and test stronger multidimensional low-pressure updates without cell floors or energy repairs. Preserve independent analytic references, conservation, divergence, limiter activity, and mesh/time studies. See docs/POSITIVITY_VERIFICATION.md and docs/EQUILIBRIUM_VERIFICATION.md. Resolve accuracy for the eventual formation regime before physical claims.
notes:
New coupled reference also requires resolved pulse-driven skin layers, compression and magnetic-shock tests. Smooth adjoint force/advection and exact global work pairing do not prove local momentum conservation at discontinuities or shock accuracy. See COUPLED_NUMERICS and COUPLED_VERIFICATION; peak flow increases 0.0661 to 0.1999 m/s over nr8 to nr32 while work is much closer to converged at fixed outer extent.
The open magnetic boundary now removes the dominant artificial outer-wall effect within measured error. Open pulse peak speeds remain 0.05919, 0.13227, 0.16262, 0.18119 m/s at nr8/16/24/32. Next numerical work should target source-driven skin layers, compression and magnetic-shock/weak-solution checks, keeping the independent loop/quadrature boundary tests and full-space energy pairing intact.
Strong cylindrical perpendicular-shock reference now exposes a false Bz reversal in the centered split (nr48 Bz/B1=-0.027288) despite conserved energy. Explicit shock_diffusion adds vanishing compressive numerical resistivity with separate heat, off by default. C=1 B-profile L1/B1 errors 0.330402, 0.218542, 0.106434, 0.0581267 at nr24/48/96/192; frozen B/rho defect is nonmonotonic and overshoot remains. Boundary/time/coefficient controls and conservative-kernel comparison retained. 99 tests pass; 20 recorded cases completed, inspected figure. Next investigate compatible fluid/magnetic numerical fluxes and conservative weak-shock/local-momentum accuracy, then skin layers; no formation claim. See SHOCK_NUMERICS and SHOCK_VERIFICATION.
New ConservativeVacuumMHD advances shared Rusanov/UCT fluid and field fluxes with existing exact magnetic vacuum. Original shock completes nr24/48/96/192; frozen-ratio defects 2.85e-6,9.22e-8,4.45e-13,9.27e-14. Positive numerical interface eta=a*h*mu0/4 and complete-update global conservative flux blend are explicit. Nonideal Poynting flux includes every adjacent face, with an independent manufactured thermal-energy check. Limiting affects 154/810 stages at nr192, so fine B/pressure profiles are worse than old split C=1 despite invariant improvement. Immediate next task: localize flux limiting while preserving local conservation, CT, admissibility and vacuum/source checks. 109 tests pass; 22 measured cases include two retained disabled-method failures. See CONSERVATIVE_COUPLING and CONSERVATIVE_VERIFICATION.
Local shared-face/corner complete-update fallback is now default, with explicit global comparison retained. Newly invalid neighbors are rechecked; no cell floors or energy repairs. 117 tests pass, including a four-pass manufactured neighbor chain, CT-only inadmissibility, independent boundary energy exchange, one-dimensional frozen ratio and actual nr96 shock locality. Original nr192 magnetic L1 improves 0.0746278 to 0.0593295; pressure L1 0.368802 to 0.334502 Pa. Limiting affects at most 0.8545 percent of cells per stage, only the outer two radial layers, with no direct reference-window replacements; frozen-ratio defect 8.06e-14. Independent response energy worsens to +0.0140806 J (5.22 percent of net outward fluid transfer), and half-CFL gives +0.0237089 J despite central profile changes below 0.00207 percent. Resolve interface/CT energy consistency next; local positivity and interior accuracy do not establish full physical validity. See LOCAL_LIMITER_VERIFICATION and INTERFACE_ENERGY_AUDIT.
Finest nr384 local shock completed at the unchanged .02 s: B/density L1 .0306517, pressure L1 .175216 Pa, frozen-ratio defect 9.72e-13, max affected fraction .4286 percent, no central-window limiting, at most two passes. But response error grows to +.0575258 J, 30.20 percent of net outward fluid energy, and numerical interface heat rises to .0984792 J. Minimum density .000388047 kg/m3, no floor; 1575 steps, 101 s setup plus 2064 s advancement. Thus interior profiles refine while interface energy does not. Twenty completed cases plus one retained disabled failure, two independent rate audits, inspected final figure. No active jobs remain. Next: use rate decomposition to fix consistent interface Poynting/CT work and reverify before moving-boundary or formation claims.
Compatible-energy work in progress: added explicit positive staggered energy, natural variational vacuum traces with actual selected CT Poynting work, and optional SSP RK3; historical defaults retained. Uniform/harmonic/thermal-work, actual shock rate and nonautonomous temporal/atomicity checks pass. Original nr192 RK3 shock response error drops from historical +0.0140806 J to +0.000596124 J. Independent quadratic RK audit predicts that residual within roundoff; stage spatial work defect <=2.20e-11 W. RK2 half-CFL error rises from .00111026 to .00218710 J, so boundary motion is not time-converged. Production 25-case study, including nr384, still running with accepted progress records; do not mark formation or interface goal complete. See COMPATIBLE_ENERGY.md and current outputs/compatible_energy_verification.
The primary compatible dataset has 24 final records (23 completed plus the disabled-limiter failure); only nr384 remains active. All four RK audits and two full-first-order nr192 time controls are complete. First-order spatial response residual drops 3.97637e-7 to 4.79246e-8 J with CFL halving, but B L1 rises to .15656 versus .05933 at second order. An exploratory uncommitted boundary-only first-order wrapper retains B L1 .059316 and yields 3.97369e-7 J at CFL .2; its half-CFL probe is still active. Do not promote that probe until formal source/pulse/boundary refinement. Its current outputs are in /private/tmp/frc-boundary-first-192-cfl*.json, separate from the frozen production study. Added independent spherical FRC/vacuum equilibrium, four analytic/topology tests, exact full-space energy quadrature and a visually reviewed reference figure. This supplies a future free-boundary test, not a formation result.
Compatible-energy checkpoint complete as progress; full FRC objective stays open. 135 tests pass in 49.04 s. All 25 main cases (24 complete, one deliberate disabled-limiter failure), two first-order time controls, six recorded boundary-strip probes and four RK audits are finished; no active numerical jobs remain. nr384 compatible RK3 finishes .02 s: B L1 .0306581, pressure .175312 Pa, response residual .00173278 J = .728851 percent of outward fluid transfer versus historical .0575258 J =30.20 percent; 1408 steps, minimum density .000916625, max affected .48489 percent, no central-window limiting. Error still grows from nr192 and half-CFL is nonmonotonic. Independent RK audit predicts nr192 error within 1.13e-12 J per step. Pulse64 error is .00315436 percent of source work versus .102119 percent historical, peak flow still unconverged. Experimental fixed first-order boundary strip retains nr192 B L1 .059316 and yields 3.97369e-7 J, then 4.78879e-8 J at half CFL; forced support is reported and this is not the default. NEXT: verify/adopt or improve this boundary treatment using source pulses, skin-layer and fine-grid/boundary controls, then free-interface evolution/actual ends and regime-appropriate transport/Hall physics. Spherical FRC analytic reference and topology/energy tests are complete but are initialized equilibrium, not formation. All source fingerprints checked; final figures inspected. Full requirement audit and remaining scope in GOAL_STATUS; Stage 2 formation gate remains closed.
Boundary validation now has 142 passing tests (57.97 s). Independent cylindrical skin reference verifies Maxwell/diffusion identities and mean surface/volume Ohmic power; physical-only, production UCT and fixed-strip runs finish nr16/32/64/128 with nr64 half-time controls. Saved-field pulse study exactly reproduces earlier standard16/32/64 budgets. Standard128 completes with peak speed .2218445 m/s and final kinetic energy .0118463 J; max adjacent64/128 velocity L2 change is 7.059 percent, so flow remains resolution-sensitive. All four end controls finished: moving gas ends ±1 to ±2 at common matching extent3 changes central velocity <.84 percent and source work ~2.1 percent; extent2-to3 alone changes flow <.000075 percent. Finest strip shock and remaining strip128/time/matching pulse records are still active. No production defaults or physical closure changed.
Completed boundary validation checkpoint as progress toward the full FRC objective. All 32 new cases finished: 12 full-field pulses through nr128, 15 analytic cylindrical skin grid/time cases, four fixed-matching gas-end controls and original nr384 strip shock. 142 tests pass in 57.97 s. Fine strip shock B L1 .03065827, p L1 .1753145 Pa, response residual 1.01130e-7 J versus standard .00173278 J; 985 steps, no additional adaptive fallback, 1534 forced/3064 affected cells, min density .0496321 without floor. But strip versus standard nr128 pulse velocity differs up to 9.767 percent; adjacent64/128 changes are 7.059 percent standard and 10.423 percent strip, with density/pressure perturbations more sensitive. No default promotion. Pulse time/magnetic-matching errors are below .001 percent, separating spatial uncertainty; moving gas ends changes central flow below .84 percent and total work about 2.1 percent. Independent skin Maxwell/diffusion/Ohmic-power tests pass; field convergence does not imply equally accurate surface current. All record/environment/NPZ hashes checked; final figure visually inspected; no jobs active. See BOUNDARY_VERIFICATION and GOAL_STATUS. NEXT: implement improved boundary/flow accuracy and moving free-interface treatment using these acceptance cases; realistic ends, transport/ionization/Hall validity, stronger shocks/cold flows/equilibrium, converged formation and dynamic UI remain required. Stage 2 gate and full goal stay open.
New ideal moving-material reference verified with exact expansion, full-space magnetized-sphere energy/force, nonuniform interior frozen-flux refinement, FRC drift and source-work time convergence. 155 tests; 26 completed evolution cases and 27 static evaluations. Explicit unresolved errors: source nr8/16 velocity differs 47.1666 percent; finite magnetic mesh gives translation force that refines ~second order but is not exactly zero; matching sphere affects spurious equilibrium flow; regular-axis/nodal advection does not preserve every interpolated material surface. No numerical viscosity/resistivity, floors or energy repair hide these issues. Gas expansion nr32 velocity error .3022 percent and initialized FRC max artificial speed .006355 m/s at .04 s. See MOVING_PLASMA_VERIFICATION. Need resistive layer/current/heat tests, broader shocks/mesh robustness and physical transport before formation interpretation.
Resistive moving verification complete with 170 tests, 13 stationary and 20 moving cases. Fixed-sphere current/local heat errors reach 0.000206685/0.000458581 at nr64 with roughly second-order convergence; Q1 B-gradient error 0.00523351 is first order. Raw midpoint falsely reverses an exact decaying semidiscrete mode despite 2.22e-16 J budget error; adaptive field/current/heat control resolves tested positive decay as tolerance tightens. Moving driven velocity still differs 63.821% at nr16/32 for D=.1; density change differs 54.0889%; D=1 is a different physical case and still has 53.915% velocity difference. Outer-time halving changes nr8 driven velocity 0.0149697%, matching radius changes nr16 velocity 0.539718%. Error is spatially unresolved, not removed by tighter energy bookkeeping. Peaks lie at/one shell inside equatorial surface; inspect heated free-surface thermodynamics, traction, modes and local current/pressure profiles. Fixed-sphere diffusion does not validate heated gas expansion into vacuum.
Continuation from clean bfd0cd8 is progress, not a wait or blocker. Saved radial profiles localize driven error to the last few equatorial shells; no obvious alternating outer-half velocity pattern. Added optional radial grading to MovingDomain, clustering material and magnetic-vacuum shells at the shared interface without changing physical D. Uniform default retains previous coordinates. Exploratory source nr8/16 grading1.5/2 job session5002 is live; no formal study yet. Next independently check graded geometry/forces/decay, record surface-refinement and angular/time controls, and retain thermal boundary limitations. Do not treat local peaks or a small energy residual as convergence.
Surface-resolution implementation and study progress: full suite 179 passed in 80.30 s; independent volume moments, exact gas expansion, sphere decay and analytic common-coordinate sampling pass. All original 20 moving + 13 reference cases finished. Supplemental nr32 grade2 CFL=.0375 cap=.000125 control remains live as session46569 after finest half-time control showed ~5.399% velocity difference. Base 17 overlap comparisons completed in terminal session14908. Direct Gauss sampling missed discontinuous thermal cell edges; exact convex-cell overlap with positive triangle quadrature now gives order4/6 agreement below 3.4e-9 relative across these base diagnostics, and independently recovers complete volume. New continuous-field velocity norm yields 34.1273% uniform16/32 and 55.2917% grade2 16/32 differences, not comparable to old vertex-lumped 63.821%. Pressure/magnetic accelerations nearly cancel at a thinning surface layer. Derived a conditional thermal compatibility defect: smooth material p=0 with continuous B and bounded div(v) requires eta J^2=0, but initial ideal FRC has nonzero edge current. Equatorial p-dot is 3.75 Pa/s unforced and 1.379547904 Pa/s source; independent finite Maxwell derivative error <4.7e-11. See SURFACE_COMPATIBILITY.md and primary sources. This is not a weak-solution nonexistence theorem. Keep original stress data, require defensible thermal/current edge model and explicit time/mesh convergence. Production/shared measurement fingerprint frozen at 2749bf18bff1bdab93b1c338b7944ec7a6773d23c39076700f83a4faec9b90c8; no core/measurement changes while supplement runs.
Surface checkpoint complete: 179 tests passed in 80.30 s; 21 dynamic + 13 independent graded cases and 18 overlap comparisons complete. Supplemental session46569 and all assembly jobs terminal. Finest grade2 time halving changes integrated velocity 5.39874%, then 2.75800% (ratio ~1.96, not asymptotic second-order evidence); current differences nonmonotonic. Quarter-time peak .5668651 m/s, min density .0555440 kg/m3, response residual 1.97602e-6 J. New integrated uniform16/32 velocity difference 34.1273%, grade2 55.2917%, fine angular 15.8362%; new norms must not overwrite old coarse-vertex 63.821%. Exact cell overlaps resolve thermal comparison quadrature; all order4/6 norm changes <3.38e-9 relative. All data/config/source/cache hashes checked, uniform baselines bitwise identical, final two figures visually inspected. See SURFACE_VERIFICATION and GOAL_STATUS. Preserve stress runs; resolve time/local momentum alongside a defensible heated-edge model.
Added independent current-inertia decay, collisionless screening and variable-coefficient continuum references. 191 tests pass; 35 recorded cases complete with source/config/field checks. de/R=.2 nr64 current error .000828866, B .00523256, local heat .00104859; inertia retains initial weak surface-current error and roughly order1.5 current convergence. Surface grading alone worsens this in the recorded control. Exact positive-Bz collisionless screening exposes false reversal at de/R=.05 nr8: minimum Bz/bias=-.00330320, negative sampled volume40.2668%, opposite current max .000978341 A/m2. Finer sampled cases remove sign artifact but nr64 B error .0730778, current .00480722. No clipping/floors/eta boost/heat cutoff. Time ratios4.002221/4.000555 from independent spatial mode; response residual <8.414e-15 of continuum energy and equations <2.341e-12 do not guarantee topology. Both figures inspected, all jobs terminal; see CURRENT_VERIFICATION.
Final current checkpoint audit supersedes the preliminary 191-test/source note: 192 tests pass in 79.10 s after fixing exact massless/zero-resistance tiny-flux cancellation under a large bias change and explicitly checking that branch Ampere residual. All 35 cases were regenerated under final frozen fingerprint c66fb837ef6af44768c87d3a88e624f9ec75e318fd24a4cfd62a82752725908f; complete source/config/archive/report checks and transport replay passed. Figures retain the same measured results and were inspected. All test, measurement, assembly and audit sessions are terminal; no live job remains. title: Demonstrate converged FRC formation experiments and honest diagnostics
description: Compare prescribed waveform families using the coupled dynamic model. Establish mesh, time, boundary and transport robustness. Separate reversal, closed flux, force balance, lifetime, model applicability and stability; retain reproducible outputs and interactive experiment controls.

title: Numerically verified and physically credible FRC experiment simulator
description:
# Active objective: a credible experimental FRC simulation

The goal is a numerically verified and physically justified simulation in which
we can vary geometry, plasma and prescribed coil waveforms to investigate FRC
formation. Passing the existing stationary-conductor tests is not completion.

## Completion evidence still required

1. Conservative axisymmetric compressible dynamics: mass, momentum, pressure/
   total energy, magnetic advection and resistivity, with compatible div B.
2. Verified plasma–vacuum coupling and suitable chamber/end/outer boundaries;
   no undisclosed conducting or massive numerical atmosphere.
3. A defensible transport/ionization model for the selected regime, with local
   scale/collisionality checks; Hall/two-fluid or kinetic treatment if required.
4. Independent tests of waves, shocks, magnetic forces, diffusion/heating and
   equilibrium preservation, including convergence and energy budgets.
5. Converged formation experiments with separate reversal, topology, force
   balance, lifetime and model-validity criteria. Robustness to time step, mesh,
   boundary and transport choices; no claim of stability from axisymmetry alone.
6. Scriptable and interactive experiments with complete reproducibility records
   and diagnostics that do not overstate the supported conclusions.

## Current evidence

The initial turn was progress: Stage 0/1 were implemented with 33 passing tests
and three waveforms plus a 27-case sweep. Their topology durations are not
converged and their illustrative argon parameters raise missing-physics warnings.

The first continuation implemented a conservative dynamic r-z MHD kernel that
passes independent cylindrical fast-wave, 2-D flux-advection, exact Sod shock,
resistive-decay/heating, axis-balance, divergence and temporal-order checks.
The next continuation added limited second-order reconstruction of fluid and
staggered magnetic traces, exact regular-axis moments, total-pressure source
integration and improved one-sided wall gradients. Smooth wave/advection errors
are much smaller; axis force accuracy improves, and a particular straight-field
polynomial equilibrium is held to roundoff. First-order comparison remains
selectable and is rerun on identical grids.
The bounded-reference checkpoint had **62 passing tests**. At identical resolution the
fast-wave error is 216 times smaller and the 2-D flux-advection error 129 times
smaller than the first-order reference on the reported benchmark grids.

An independent continuum Grad–Shafranov fixture now tests genuinely curved,
closed poloidal flux with reversed Bz. It starts in equilibrium, not from coil
formation. Its artificial motion decreases with refinement, but it is not held
exactly. A lower-pressure p0=0.1 Pa stress case previously failed reconstruction
on coarse meshes despite positive cell pressure. That failure is now fixed by
local admissibility reconstruction, with consistent geometric-source integration.
Cell averages and magnetic traces are unchanged by this limiter; there are no
cell floors or energy repairs. The original failure remains reproducible with
the explicit disable switch. Limiting affects 12.10% and 2.19% of accepted
cell-stages at nr=12/24, and zero at nr=48/96 in that fixture.
The default p0=1 Pa case completes across refinement after correcting the wall
derivative. Smooth temporal refinement verifies RK2; the quarter-period wave's
limiter-switching time ratios are separately retained and less regular.
For p0=1 Pa, the finest 192×384 equilibrium run has maximum artificial speed
0.00095046 times the reference Alfvén speed after 0.1 s, with flux relative L2
drift 2.1181e-5. The initial force volume RMS converges at approximately order
1.5, so this remains a measured limitation rather than exact equilibrium balance.
Fixed-grid time refinement barely changes that drift, confirming that spatial
error dominates this particular case. Mass/energy and face divergence remain
at floating-point accuracy. Generated figures were visually inspected.

Additional equilibrium stress cases down to p0=1e-5 Pa finish conservatively,
but their coarse-grid artificial motion is not physical accuracy evidence.
An independently solved magnetized double rarefaction remains positive and
conservative with unchanged uniform B. Its bulk L1 errors converge, while the
central pressure is still 114% too high at 640 axial cells. The admissibility
limiter is inactive there: this exposes underlying flux-discretization error,
not a pressure floor. It is tracked as an accuracy requirement, not hidden by
the passing positivity checks. No full-update positivity theorem is claimed.

Measured evidence is in `docs/MHD_VERIFICATION.md`,
`docs/EQUILIBRIUM_VERIFICATION.md`, `docs/POSITIVITY_VERIFICATION.md`, and their
JSON/plot outputs. The limiter derivation is `docs/POSITIVITY.md`. These remain
bounded verification solvers, not the coupled coil-driven formation experiment.

## Dynamic vacuum coupling checkpoint

That coupling checkpoint had **74 passing tests** (18.08 s).
`VacuumCoupledMHD` advances compressible gas inside a fixed, gas-filled chamber
with reflecting slip walls/ends and magnetically transparent boundaries. A
larger magnetic-only exterior satisfies the elliptic induced-current constraint;
there are no exterior density, pressure or conductivity degrees of freedom.
An adjoint magnetic force/advection pair, implicit midpoint and gas Euler Strang
splitting account for induced self-field energy, gas energy, prescribed-source
work and positive physical Ohmic heat. This response-energy budget excludes
external-field self/mutual energy and is not a coil-circuit energy estimate.
Failure leaves accepted state, time and cumulative work intact. A source time
cap is explicit because fluid CFL cannot discover arbitrary short pulses.

Independent compact-field J cross B errors decrease from 0.2707 to 0.006437 in
volume L2 as radial resolution increases 8→64, including axis cells. Passive
advection errors decrease 0.008325→0.002155→0.0005438 at 12/24/48 cells; Gaussian
resistive-diffusion errors decrease 0.007174→0.001822→0.0004573. Fixed-grid time
halving reduces momentum error by 4.010 and 4.050. A separate infinite-space
circular-loop integral distinguishes mesh error from magnetic-box error:
at 32 cells/m, zero-flux outer extents 2/4/8 m give 5.429%, 0.6791%, 0.08840%
probe error. With independent exact boundary data the 32-cell/m error is 0.03344%.

Two prescribed coils now induce current, gas acceleration and heat in this
reference. Across the reported dynamic cases the maximum relative response-
energy residual is 1.63e-14; mass change is at most 1.42e-16. Compatible face
divergence is near roundoff. **Pulse flow is not yet converged:** final peak speed
increases 0.0661→0.1473→0.1798→0.1999 m/s at 8/16/24/32 radial cells. The magnetic
boundary also matters: at 16 cells, extent 2→4 m changes final source work by
about 19%, and 3→4 m still changes it by about 3.8%. A small solver residual is
therefore not physical boundary accuracy. Figures were inspected; full inputs,
histories, source fingerprint and versions are retained with the report.

See `docs/COUPLED_NUMERICS.md`, `docs/COUPLED_VERIFICATION.md` and
`outputs/coupled_verification/metrics.json`. Earlier reports remain historical
measurements of their recorded source, not reruns with this different solver.

## Current development step

The magnetic boundary requirement has progressed with the verified infinite
exterior described below. The new shock study exposes false magnetic reversal
in the centered split and measures an explicit vanishing diffusion option.
An unsplit conservative fluid/UCT implementation now couples through the same
vacuum and preserves the tested interior frozen-flux relation. Prioritize
localizing its full-update flux limiter and extending shock/interface-work
verification, alongside source-driven skin-layer resolution. Its global limiter
is active on finer cold-boundary grids and affects otherwise smooth interior
accuracy. The historical split diffusion option remains a comparison. Replace the
fixed gas-filled interface with a defensible
evolving plasma–vacuum treatment before interpreting detached torus formation.
Validate actual chamber/end conditions, transport and Hall applicability. The
fixed-chamber reference is useful measured progress, not completion of
`frc-vacuum`. `Experiment(stage=2)` stays gated.
Cold-flow pressure accuracy, curved-equilibrium stress balance and stronger
full-update robustness remain tracked separately. Transport applicability can
be developed alongside numerical coupling without selecting arbitrary closure.

## Infinite magnetic exterior checkpoint

That checkpoint had **83 passing tests** (20.90 s). The preceding turn
made verified progress, with no external job remaining live at this checkpoint.
`vacuum_boundary="multipole"` now represents the induced magnetic field to
infinity using regular-axis decaying Legendre modes. Boundary nodal traces,
interior magnetic energy and an independently integrated exterior energy form
one symmetric matrix. Exterior nodes and modal amplitudes satisfy stationary
vacuum rows; modes have no fluid mass, current density or resistivity. The
midpoint response-energy budget includes energy beyond the field grid.
The historical fixed zero-flux boundary remains an explicit comparison.

Independent displaced toroidal-current quadrature excites both odd and even
modes. Interior flux relative L2 errors at 8/16/32/64 fluid radial cells are
0.01257, 0.0008744, 0.0001845 and 0.00004552. Interior/exterior normal-derivative
mismatch decreases 0.01653→0.003882→0.0009413→0.0002318, including matching-surface
corners. Exterior B error at fixed 32 cells drops from 32.3% with one mode to
about 0.0364% with twelve; higher modes then reach the spatial-error plateau.
A separate analytic dipole and independent all-space volume integral check
normalization, axis fields and the sign/magnitude of exterior magnetic energy.

All fixed/open pulse comparisons were rerun from current code. At 16 fluid radial
cells and 12 multipoles, moving the matching rectangle from 2 to 4 m changes
source work by **0.00206%**. The corresponding fixed-wall change is **23.646%**,
using the 4 m result as denominator for both percentages. The prior roughly 19%
figure used the 2 m fixed-wall result as denominator. Open pulse energy residuals
are at most 2.21e-14 relative to initial response energy; mass change is at most
2.83e-16 and modal stationarity residual at most 6.32e-13. Beyond-grid magnetic
energy is positive and included. No exterior fluid or state repair is introduced.

The pulse still is not spatially converged: open-boundary final peak speeds are
0.05919, 0.13227, 0.16262 and 0.18119 m/s at 8/16/24/32 cells. At 16 cells,
halving CFL changes source work by about 0.046%, larger than the measured boundary
surface effect. More modes alone cannot fix fluid or time-discretization error.
The current single-center expansion requires a matching rectangle enclosing the
entire chamber's source sphere; efficiency for long chambers remains to evaluate.

Derivation, measured results, inspected figure, complete inputs/histories and
source fingerprint are in `docs/OPEN_BOUNDARY.md`,
`docs/OPEN_BOUNDARY_VERIFICATION.md`, and
`outputs/open_boundary_verification/metrics.json`. This verifies the open
**magnetic** exterior, not a moving free plasma surface, gas outflow, transport,
magnetic shocks or FRC formation. `frc-vacuum` and the full objective stay active.

## Magnetic shock and implicit solver checkpoint

That checkpoint had **99 passing tests** (25.17 s). That continuation made
verified progress; all measurement/report jobs completed, with none left live.

An independent strong perpendicular shock now has exact Rankine–Hugoniot jumps
and steady cylindrical branches. Finite-difference momentum and invariant checks
validate the reference independently of the numerical kernels. Both actual 2-D
solvers are tested in an interior annulus before remote boundaries dominate.
The centered coupled method creates a **false Bz reversal** at nr=48, reaching
Bz/B1=-0.027288 even with a relative response-energy residual around 1e-14.
Such magnetic structure must not be interpreted as FRC topology.

The explicit `shock_diffusion` option adds a nonnegative compressive diffusivity
that scales as h² in smooth flow and h at shocks. It is off by default and
separately records numerical magnetic heat, without changing physical Ohmic
heat or putting fluid/resistivity in vacuum. No cell floors or energy repair are
introduced. With C=1, magnetic-profile L1/B1 errors at nr=24/48/96/192 are
0.330402, 0.218542, 0.106434, 0.0581267; density errors are 0.299483, 0.187281,
0.0960794, 0.046949 kg/m³; pressure errors are 1.93626, 1.06167, 0.574753,
0.190947 Pa. No false sign reversal occurs in those C=1 windows. However,
frozen B/rho error is **not monotonic**, and nr=192 still overshoots Bz/B1 to
3.6293 versus the physical shock value 3.53234. The conservative bounded
reference preserves that special B/rho invariant to roundoff. More diffusion
is not uniformly more accurate; the coefficient study retains that tradeoff.

At nr=48, moving the inner nonanalytic extension changes pressure/B profiles by
0.3302%/0.08888% in relative L2. Doubling chamber length changes profiles below
7.1e-9; a shorter 0.01 s wall-taper control gives density change 4.86e-5.
CFL halving changes the B profile by 1.43e-5, then 3.45e-6. These are measured
controls at that grid/window/time, not general free-boundary verification.
Maximum coupled response-energy residual is 1.94e-14, mass change 2.19e-16,
and face divergence 1.25e-16 T/m. Numerical magnetic heat remains explicitly
reported (0.433 J at nr=192 for the whole chamber); physical eta and heat are
zero. Entropy-producing shock dissipation need not vanish with grid spacing.

The midpoint solve now defaults to a cached-vacuum Picard iteration at tolerance
1e-13. It solves the same implicit equations and retains atomic failure. The
original direct solve remains selectable. Direct/Picard tests cover both
magnetic boundaries and independent physical/numerical diffusion choices. Their
nr=24 shock profiles agree within 9.9e-13 relative L2; measured advance time is
6.96 times faster for Picard in that fixture. This is a CPU wall-time measurement,
not a GPU or general real-time claim.

The inspected six-panel figure, 20 completed cases, complete configuration,
initial/final diagnostics, profiles, environment and source fingerprints are in
`docs/SHOCK_VERIFICATION.md`, `docs/SHOCK_NUMERICS.md`, and
`outputs/shock_verification/metrics.json`. Old reports retain historical hashes.
Next, investigate the split method's inconsistent magnetic/fluid numerical flux
and local momentum/weak-shock accuracy, while preserving the verified vacuum
and work identities. Continue the unresolved cold rarefaction, equilibrium,
skin-layer, free-interface, transport and formation requirements below.

## Conservative fluid/CT coupling checkpoint

The current full suite has **109 passing tests** (32.92 s). This continuation is
